messages:
emily: Alert from infra-monitor: found a firewall rule in project `redwood-staging` allowing 0.0.0.0/0 TCP:6379 -> subnet `prod-like-redis-staging`. tagging as potential public redis exposure. https://console.cloud.google.com/networking/firewalls/details?project=redwood-staging

raj: ack. do we know who created it and when?

emily: rule name `allow-redis-ingress-temp`, created ~8m ago by serviceAccount: deployer-sa@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com per audit log. severity medium for now.

liz: curious if this was a terraform drift or manual console change. can someone run `gcloud compute firewall-rules describe allow-redis-ingress-temp --project=redwood-staging --format=json` and paste output?

emily: pasted output below:
```
{
  "name": "allow-redis-ingress-temp",
  "network": "projects/redwood-staging/global/networks/prod-like-vpc",
  "allowed": [{"IPProtocol": "tcp", "ports": ["6379"]}],
  "sourceRanges": ["0.0.0.0/0"],
  "targetTags": ["redis-staging"],
  "creationTimestamp": "2026-03-20T15:34:10.000Z",
  "fingerprint": "..."
}
```

dennis: immediate containment: remove 0.0.0.0/0 or reduce to internal CIDR. propose `gcloud compute firewall-rules update allow-redis-ingress-temp --source-ranges=10.0.0.0/8 --project=redwood-staging` then set a deny rule for anything else.

raj: +1. also rotate any redis AUTH tokens if there are recent external connections. run `gcloud logging read "resource.type=gce_instance AND protoPayload.request.methodName=\"Compute.firewalls.insert\" AND resource.labels.project_id=\"redwood-staging\"" --project=redwood-staging --limit=50` to pull related logs.

emily: containment applied: changed sourceRanges to 10.0.0.0/8 and added a higher-priority deny rule. firewall shows updated at 15:38 UTC. tagging incident tracker: INC-2026-042.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created and assigned to eng-security. SLA timer started.

liz: good. next: check redis logs for external IPs to port 6379 in last 24h. dennis, can you run `gcloud logging read "logName=\"projects/redwood-staging/logs/redis-access\" AND jsonPayload.remote_ip:6379" --project=redwood-staging --limit=200` and paste suspicious IPs?

dennis: ran. saw three connections from 52.23.12.9, 18.205.44.1, and one internal 10.4.3.7 between 15:30-15:36 UTC. external IPs look like cloud provider ranges.

raj: check if deployer-sa has broad IAM perms. `gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy deployer-sa@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-staging`

emily: policy shows deployer-sa has roles/compute.networkAdmin + roles/iam.serviceAccountUser. that's too permissive for a deployer. looks like a runaway adhoc permission escalation during a rollout.

liz: if deployer-sa created rule, rotate keys and restrict the service account. revoke long-lived keys if any and restrict to scoped ephemeral credentials only. dennis: can you disable new token issuance for that SA and create a scoped short-lived mTLS token for the rollout pipeline?

dennis: disabling legacy keys now. flagged 1 JSON key -> marked for revocation. added conditional IAM binding to require `request.auth.claims.pipeline==true` (we'll formalize).

raj: verify KMS usage: any KMS keys used by redis secrets exposed? `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy redis-secret-key --location=global --keyring=secrets --project=redwood-secrets`

emily: checked KMS access log, no direct decrypts from external IPs. redis AUTH still protected by KMS and Cloud SQL-style secret manager. no evidence KMS key compromised.

liz: good. next actions for post-incident: 1) Terraform drift detection -> enable Config Connector/Policy to prevent firewall with 0.0.0.0/0 on redis ports. 2) Lockdown deployer-sa perms and move to short-lived signing key via workload identity. 3) Add logging alert for any firewall creation with sourceRanges=0.0.0.0/0 on redis tag. 4) Rotate redis auth secrets and audit access.

emily: will open RFC for the three changes and link INC-2026-042. assigning myself for rotation + terraform guard; dennis will handle SA hardening; raj will add log-based alert and incident writeup.

oncall-bot: Reminder: please add postmortem within 72 hours for INC-2026-042.

dennis: quick note: found a PR in infra repo that temporarily whitelists 0.0.0.0/0 for testing, merged by mistake. adding branch protection + require reviewers from infra-team.

raj: thanks. adding follow-up tasks to the tracker and scheduling 30-min postmortem sync tomorrow.

emily: closing loop: no evidence of data exfil or persisted compromise. external connections from cloud IPs look like an automated scanner hitting the open port during the ~6-minute window. will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
